messages.author: 0f36a4d38f68e366
messages.subject: Re: some questions with msstats
parts:
Yes, you can. Assuming data.res is the output from groupComparisonTMT(), try the following code:

 libarary(MSstats)
 ## profile plot
  data.res$Tvalue <-data.res$log2FC/data.res$SE
  groupComparisonPlots(data=data.res, type="VolcanoPlot", FCcutoff = 2,
                       logBase.pvalue=2)

  # Comparison Plot
  groupComparisonPlots(data=data.res, type="ComparisonPlot")

messages.author: 0f36a4d38f68e366
messages.subject: Re: some questions with msstats
parts:
Yes, you can use the same function but change the type to Heatmap.

 libarary(MSstats)
 ## Heatmap of adjusted p-values for multiple comparisons
  data.res$Tvalue <-data.res$log2FC/data.res$SE
  groupComparisonPlots(data=data.res, type="Heatmap", FCcutoff = 2,
                       logBase.pvalue=2)

messages.author: 0f36a4d38f68e366
messages.subject: Re: some questions with msstats
parts: It seems that heatmap function from MSstats is not applicable to your data. Because heatmaps in MSstats require at least two comparisons but your data has only one comparison (ACO-HA). The heatmaps in MSstats is to illustrate up-/down-regulated proteins for multiple comparisons with all proteins. Each row represents each protein. Each column represents each comparison of interest. So it needs at least two columns (two comparisons).
